item.title: Timeouts, retries and circuit breakers with Resilience4j
item.description: In a system of services, a dependency that is down is the easy case: the call fails quickly and you handle the error. The hard case is a dependency that is slow. Every call waits. Threads pile up waiting. The calling service runs out of threads and stops responding. Now its callers are waiting. One slow database query turns into an outage three services away. The tools for this are old and well known: timeouts, retries, circuit breakers, bulkheads.

item.title: Moving data off a legacy platform without a big bang
item.description: Moving code from a legacy platform to new services is the part everyone talks about. With the gateway in front, you can route one endpoint at a time to the new service. Moving the data is harder, because for a while it has to live in two places, and both places think they’re right. The “big bang” version: announce downtime for a weekend, stop everything, run a migration script, switch, hope.

item.title: Contract tests: how services stop breaking each other
item.description: With one monolith, if you rename a field, the compiler tells you everywhere it’s used. With twenty services, nobody tells you. Your tests pass, your service deploys, and another service that reads that field starts failing in production. The compiler’s job is now yours. The usual answers are not great: Unit tests with mocks test your service against your idea of the other service. If your idea is wrong, the tests are green and wrong.

item.title: One door for every client: an API gateway as a facade
item.description: As we split the old platform into Spring Boot services, we got a new problem very quickly: there are now many services, and many kinds of clients. The web app, the assessment UI, LMS integrations, the clients used on board ships. If every client talks to every service directly, every client has to know where every service lives, how it authenticates, and how its API looks this month. So all clients go through one entry point: an API gateway that acts as a facade over the services behind it.
